mainTopic: The laws of יחוד, the punishments connected to it, and stories about the strength of the יצר הרע
overview: This amud is about יחוד, a man and a woman being alone together. רב rules that two men with a woman are enough in a city, but on the road you need three. The גמרא tries to prove this from the סוטה case and rejects the proof. In a story, רב is strict even with himself and רב יהודה, explaining that 'upright men' means people like רבי חנינא בר פפי. רב rules that בית דין flogs for יחוד, and רב אשי limits this to an unmarried woman so no rumors spread about a married woman's children. רב also allows flogging for a bad rumor. The גמרא then lists cases where יחוד is not a concern: the husband in town, an open door to the street, and room setups, where a ברייתא disagrees with רב כהנא and אביי is strict both ways. Stories about רב עמרם חסידא, רבי מאיר, רבי עקיבא and פלימו show how strong the יצר הרע is. פלימו's story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The scholars know how to warn him
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous answer: the two escorts must be תלמידי חכמים so they know how to warn the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...to warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer from the previous page. The escorts of the סוטה's husband must be תלמידי חכמים because they know how to properly warn him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people might not know how to give a proper warning (התראה). Scholars do, so they can stop the husband from being with his wife on the way, which would spoil the test of the bitter waters.

phrases.english: to warn him.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: the scholars are needed because they know how to warn the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַתְרוֹיֵי בֵּיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The escorts must be scholars because they know how to warn the husband.

steps.title: On the road, three men are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: two men with one woman is fine only in a city. On the road, three are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They only taught this in a city. But on the road, there must be three, because one of them may need to step away to relieve himself, and then one man is left alone with a forbidden woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב limits the rule that a woman may be alone with two men. That rule works in a city, but on the road you need three men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is practical. On the road, if one of two men steps away to relieve himself, the other is left alone with the woman. With three men, even if one leaves, two remain.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of... (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה of יחוד: the number of men needed changes depending on where they are.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They taught this only in a city,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that one woman may be alone with two men.

phrases.english: but on the road, not until there are three,
in case one of them needs to urinate,
and it turns out that one is alone with the forbidden woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בָּעִיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two men with one woman is allowed only in a city. On the road, three men are required.

steps.title: A suggested proof from the סוטה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the סוטה case supports רב: the husband plus two scholars makes three on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? 'They give him two Torah scholars, in case he is with her on the way.' Two plus him makes three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to support רב's rule from the סוטה case. On the road, the husband travels with two scholars, which adds up to three men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by counting. If the law gave the husband exactly two escorts on a journey, it seems the law wants three men there, just like רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
They hand over to him, they assign him

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
They assign him two Torah scholars
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה about the husband bringing his סוטה wife to ירושלים.

phrases.english: in case he has relations with her on the road.
Two and him, that makes three!

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support רב's rule
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that three men are needed on the road
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סוטה case: the husband plus two scholars on the journey

steps.title: The two scholars are there as witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: in the סוטה case, two scholars are needed so they can serve as witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is so that they can be witnesses against him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The סוטה case needs two scholars for a different reason: testimony requires two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number two in the סוטה case is not about יחוד at all. It is about having a full set of witnesses (two) who can testify whether he was with her. So nothing can be learned from it about needing three men.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנִיהְווֹ עֲלֵיהּ סָהֲדִי.
phrases.english: There, it is so that they will be witnesses about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנִיהְווֹ עֲלֵיהּ סָהֲדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רב's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two scholars are needed as a pair of witnesses, not to prevent יחוד.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (three on the road) stands on its own reasoning. The סוטה case does not prove it, because there the two are needed as witnesses.

steps.title: רב tells רב יהודה to hurry away
steps.stepSummary: A story: a woman walked ahead of רב and רב יהודה on the road, and רב told רב יהודה to walk faster, away from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רב יהודה were walking on the road, and a woman was walking ahead of them. רב said to רב יהודה: Lift your feet away from גיהנם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב himself. He wanted to get away from a woman walking near them, calling the situation 'גיהנם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though there were two men, רב did not want to stay near the woman on the road. The story sets up a question: doesn't this contradict רב's own lenient ruling?

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַב יְהוּדָה הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: Rav and Rav Yehuda were walking on the road,
a certain woman was walking ahead of them.
Rav said to Rav Yehuda:
Lift your feet away from Gehinnom.
phrases.notes: He means: let's hurry past her, so we don't end up in a situation that leads to sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַב יְהוּדָה הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב acted strictly and moved away from a woman on the road, even with two men present.

steps.title: Didn't you allow it for trustworthy men?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges רב: you yourself said that for upright men it is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But isn't it you, Master, who said that with upright men it is fine?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה points out that רב seems to be contradicting his own ruling. רב had said that for men of good character, this is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had ruled leniently for כשרים, men of good character. רב יהודה assumes the two of them are certainly כשרים, so why be strict now?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it you, Master, who said...
It is fine, it is allowed

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it you, Master, who said
that with upright men it is fine!
phrases.notes: רב had ruled earlier that a woman being alone with two men is allowed when they are upright men.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר בִּכְשֵׁרִים שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's behavior in the story
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's strict behavior on the road
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself allowed this for upright men, and surely he and רב יהודה are upright.

steps.title: Who says we count as upright?
steps.stepSummary: רב answers: who says that 'upright' means people like you and me?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who says that 'upright' means people like you and me?
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that his lenient ruling was not about people like himself and רב יהודה. The word 'upright' means something higher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction, because 'כשרים' is a very high level of trust. Even great scholars like רב and רב יהודה do not automatically count for this leniency.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב is saying they are bad people. He is saying the leniency is for an extraordinary level of self-control, not just good people.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who says
that 'upright men' means ones like me and you?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי יֵימַר דְּבִכְשֵׁרִים כְּגוֹן אֲנָא וְאַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any good, learned person counts as 'upright'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Upright' means a much higher level than even רב and רב יהודה.

steps.title: Then who does count?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks: if not us, then like whom?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, like whom?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks who does count as 'upright' for this rule. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב said they do not qualify, the natural question is who does. This asks for the definition of the category.

phrases.english: Rather, like whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן מַאי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who qualifies as כשרים for this leniency?

steps.title: Like רבי חנינא בר פפי and his friends
steps.stepSummary: רב answers: people like רבי חנינא בר פפי and his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי חנינא בר פפי and his colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: רב names who counts as 'upright': רבי חנינא בר פפי and people of his level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were people known for resisting temptation. So the leniency of 'upright men' applies only to people of that rare, proven level.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage known for holding back from sin

steps.whatToRemember: The leniency for 'upright men' applies only to people on the level of רבי חנינא בר פפי. That is why רב was strict even with himself and רב יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי וַחֲבֵירָיו.
phrases.english: Like Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi and his colleagues.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי וַחֲבֵירָיו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only people like רבי חנינא בר פפי and his colleagues count as כשרים.

steps.title: Flogging for יחוד, but no prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב rules: the court flogs for יחוד, but יחוד does not make a woman forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They flog for יחוד, but they do not forbid a woman because of יחוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new ruling about the result of יחוד. The man is punished with lashes, but the woman does not become forbidden because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being alone together is wrong in itself, so it deserves punishment. But it is not proof that they actually sinned, so a wife stays permitted to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and woman being alone together

steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two things: the sin of being alone together, and the question of whether something forbidden actually happened.

phrases.english: Rav said: They flog for being alone together,
but they do not forbid a woman because of being alone together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַלְקִין עַל יִיחוּד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחוד brings lashes, but does not make the woman forbidden.

steps.title: No flogging for יחוד with a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits רב's rule: flogging is only for יחוד with an unmarried woman. With a married woman there is no flogging, so no rumors spread about her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We only said this about יחוד with an unmarried woman. But for יחוד with a married woman, no, so that there should not be rumors about her children.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows רב's rule. Flogging for יחוד applies only with an unmarried woman, not a married one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the court flogged a man for being alone with a married woman, people would assume they sinned. Then her children might be suspected of being ממזרים. To protect them, there is no flogging in that case.
steps.whatToRemember: Flogging for יחוד applies only with an unmarried woman. With a married woman the court holds back, to protect her children from rumors.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We said this only about being alone with an unmarried woman,
but for being alone with a married woman, no,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא מוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל בָּנֶיהָ.
phrases.english: so that you should not spread a bad rumor about her children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּיִיחוּד פְּנוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's ruling about flogging
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flogging for יחוד applies only with an unmarried woman. With a married woman there is no flogging, to protect her children's reputation.

steps.title: מר זוטרא flogs and announces the reason
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא used to flog for יחוד and publicly announce why.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא would flog, and he would announce the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how מר זוטרא handled flogging for יחוד. It sets up the next question to רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי limited flogging to an unmarried woman, so no rumors would spread about a married woman's children. מר זוטרא flogged even in the married-woman case, but he announced that it was only for יחוד. The announcement protects the woman's name.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra would flog and announce.
phrases.notes: He flogged even for יחוד with a married woman, and announced that it was only for יחוד, not for adultery.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מַלְקֵי וּמַכְרֵיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a different practice from רב אשי's limit in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may flog for יחוד even with a married woman, as long as the reason is announced.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב אשי also flog and announce?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן מפרהטיא asks רב אשי to follow מר זוטרא's method.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן from פרהטיא said to רב אשי: Let the master also flog and announce!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן מפרהטיא challenges רב אשי. If announcing solves the rumor problem, רב אשי should also flog in the married-woman case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's only reason for not flogging was the fear of rumors about the children. מר זוטרא's announcement seems to remove that fear. So רב אשי's limit looks unnecessary.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן מִפַּרְהַטְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman from Parhatya said to Rav Ashi:
Let the master also flog and announce!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר נָמֵי לַילְקֵי וְלַכְרֵיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses מר זוטרא's practice to challenge רב אשי's limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule of not flogging for יחוד with a married woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Announcing the reason removes the rumor problem, so there is no need to hold back the flogging.

steps.title: Some will hear the flogging but not the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the announcement does not reach everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There are people who will hear about this and not hear about that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends his rule. Some people will hear that a man was flogged but miss the announcement explaining why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those people may assume adultery happened, and rumors about the children would spread anyway. So the announcement does not fully fix the problem, and רב אשי's limit stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: There are those who hear about this,
phrases.notes: "This" is the flogging.

phrases.english: and do not hear about that.
phrases.notes: "That" is the announcement explaining the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּשָׁמַע בְּהָא וְלָא שָׁמַע בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical limit: the announcement does not reach everyone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Announcing the reason fully stops the rumors.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some people hear only about the flogging, so rumors could still spread. Better not to flog in the married-woman case.
steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא flogged and announced the reason. רב אשי did not flog in the married-woman case, because not everyone hears the announcement.

steps.title: Flogging because of a bad rumor
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the court may flog someone who has a bad rumor about him, based on a פסוק about עלי's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: We flog because of a rumor that is not good, as it says: "No, my sons, for it is not a good report."
steps.whatsHappening: רב brings a new rule. בית דין may give lashes to someone who has a bad reputation, even without full proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is עלי's rebuke of his sons, where he scolds them because of what people are saying. This connects to יחוד: flogging for יחוד is also flogging for suspicious behavior, not for a proven sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A report that is not good, a bad rumor

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בית דין can punish to stop bad behavior and protect the community, not only for proven sins.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מַלְקִין עַל לֹא טוֹבָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה,
phrases.english: Rav says: We flog because of a report that is not good,
as it is stated: "No, my sons,
for it is not a good report."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:24

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַלְקִין עַל לֹא טוֹבָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related flogging rule after the discussion of flogging for יחוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין may flog someone because of a bad rumor about him.

steps.title: How מר זוטרא carried out the flogging
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא put a donkey's bridle on the person's shoulder and recited the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא would put a bridle on his shoulder and read to him: "No, my sons."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how מר זוטרא carried out רב's rule of flogging for a bad rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bridle was a public sign of shame. Reading the פסוק let everyone know the lashes were for a bad rumor and not for a proven sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A bridle, the strap used to lead a donkey

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא מוֹתֵיב לֵהּ אַפְסֵירָה עַל כַּתְפֵּיהּ
phrases.english: Mar Zutra would place a bridle on his shoulder
and recite to him: "No, my sons."
phrases.notes: He means the whole פסוק from רב's statement, so everyone knew why he was flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מוֹתֵיב לֵהּ אַפְסֵירָה עַל כַּתְפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב's rule was put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When flogging for a bad rumor, make the reason public by reciting the פסוק.

steps.title: Her husband is in town
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if the woman's husband is in town, there is no concern of יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: If her husband is in the city, we are not concerned about יחוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lists cases where יחוד is not a concern. רבה gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband is nearby, the man is afraid he might walk in at any moment. That fear keeps him from sinning, so being alone together is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and woman being alone together in private

phrases.english: Rabba says: If her husband is in town,
we are not concerned about seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בַּעְלָהּ בָּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new list of cases where יחוד is not a concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband is in town, יחוד with his wife is not a concern.

steps.title: A door open to the street
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that an open door to the public area removes the concern of יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: If there is a door open to the public domain, we are not concerned about יחוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a second case where יחוד is not a concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the door opens to a public area, anyone passing might look in. That chance of being seen keeps people from sinning.

keyTerms.meaning: Public domain, a place where many people pass

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: פֶּתַח פָּתוּחַ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים –
phrases.english: Rav Yosef says: If there is an entrance open to the public domain,
we are not concerned about seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: פֶּתַח פָּתוּחַ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case where יחוד is not a concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An entrance open to the public domain removes the concern of יחוד.

steps.title: רב ביבי asks to remove the ladder
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי visited רב יוסף's house and asked them to remove the ladder so he could not come down at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי came to רב יוסף's house. After eating, he said to them: Take away the ladder from under ביבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how carefully רב ביבי guarded himself from יחוד. This story sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ביבי slept upstairs and had the ladder removed so he could not come down to where רב יוסף's wife was. He was protecting himself from יחוד even though רב יוסף was in town.

phrases.aramaic: רַב בִּיבִי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Rav Beivai came to Rav Yosef's house.
After he ate his meal, he said to them:
Take away the ladder from under Beivai.
phrases.notes: He was sleeping upstairs and is talking about himself, so he couldn't climb down at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that seems to go against רבה's rule in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי was careful about יחוד in רב יוסף's house.

steps.title: But רבה said a husband in town is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ביבי was worried, since רב יוסף was in town.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה said: If her husband is in town, we are not concerned about יחוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story using רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף, the husband, was in town. According to רבה there should be no concern, so removing the ladder seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabba say: If her husband is in town,
we are not concerned about seclusion!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה: בַּעְלָהּ בָּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story in step 19 based on רבה's rule in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי's extra caution in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband was in town, so by רבה's rule there was nothing to worry about.

steps.title: רב ביבי was close with her
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's wife was a close friend of רב ביבי and comfortable with him, so the usual rule did not protect enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי is different, because she was his friend and was familiar with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב ביבי's case was special, so רבה's rule still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's rule works because a stranger is afraid to sin. When the man and woman already know each other well, that fear is weaker, so extra care is needed even when the husband is in town.

keyTerms.meaning: She was familiar and at ease with him

steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject רבה's rule. It only says the rule doesn't cover a man and woman who are already close.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai is different,
since she was his friend and was familiar with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַב בִּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ביבי's caution goes against רבה's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה's rule holds in general, but not when the man and woman are close and familiar with each other.

steps.title: Men outside, women inside
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that if the men are in the outer room and the women in the inner room, there is no concern of יחוד, but the reverse is a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא says: Men outside and women inside, we are not concerned about יחוד. Men inside and women outside, we are concerned about יחוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adds another case about יחוד and compares two room setups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the women are in the inner room, any man going in must pass the other men and would be seen. If the men are inside, one can say he is leaving and actually go to the women, so יחוד is a concern.
steps.whatToRemember: Cases with no concern of יחוד so far: her husband is in town (unless the two are close), and a door open to the street. רב כהנא's room rule does not stand as final: the next step brings a ברייתא that says the reverse, and אביי ends up strict in both room setups.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אֲנָשִׁים מִבַּחוּץ וְנָשִׁים מִבִּפְנִים –
phrases.english: Rav Kahana says: If the men are outside and the women inside,
we are not concerned about seclusion.
If the men are inside and the women outside,
we are concerned about seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אֲנָשִׁים מִבַּחוּץ וְנָשִׁים מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of יחוד cases from steps 17 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Men outside and women inside is not a concern of יחוד. Men inside and women outside is a concern.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the opposite of רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reverses רב כהנא's rule about which room arrangement raises a concern of יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a ברייתא it was taught the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא says the exact opposite of what רב כהנא just ruled. This sets up אביי's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא said men outside and women inside is fine, but the reverse is a problem. The ברייתא flips it: men outside and women inside is a problem, but men inside and women outside is fine. Now we have two sources that contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: In a baraita it was taught the opposite.
phrases.notes: The opposite of רב כהנא's rule in step 22: here men outside with women inside is the worrying case.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that contradicts רב כהנא's ruling in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling about men in the outer room and women in the inner room.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the reverse arrangement is the safe one, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי decides to be strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: Since the two sources disagree, אביי will be strict in both arrangements.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Now that רב כהנא said it this way and the ברייתא taught the opposite, I will act strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction for his own practice by being strict in both arrangements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not choose one opinion over the other. Each source says a different arrangement is risky, so he treats both arrangements as a concern of יחוד. That way he is covered no matter which source is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: To the strict side, acting stringently

steps.whatToRemember: When רב כהנא and the ברייתא disagree about which room setup is safe, אביי is strict in both, so neither setup is fully trusted.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Now that Rav Kahana said this way
and a baraita taught the opposite,
I will act stringently.
phrases.notes: He means strict in both setups, since each source worries about a different one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא הָכִי וְתָנָא מַתְנִיתָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 23 in practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, both arrangements of men and women in inner and outer rooms are treated strictly.

steps.title: How אביי and רבא separated men and women
steps.stepSummary: אביי set up rows of pitchers and רבא set up rows of reeds to separate men and women.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would arrange rows of pitchers. רבא would arrange rows of reeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us the practical barriers אביי and רבא used to keep men and women apart at gatherings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitchers and reeds would make noise or block the way if someone tried to cross from one side to the other. This puts אביי's strict approach into practice with a physical barrier.

phrases.english: Abaye would arrange rows of pitchers.
phrases.notes: He set them between the men and the women, so anyone crossing would knock them and make noise.

phrases.english: Rava would arrange rows of reeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי דָּיַיר גּוּלְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the strict approach was carried out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A physical, noisy barrier should separate men and women at gatherings.

steps.title: The festival is the riskiest time of year
steps.stepSummary: אבין says the weak spot of the year is the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבין said: The wound of the year is the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: אבין explains why these barriers matter so much: the festival is the time when people are most likely to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a רגל, men and women gather together in a happy, relaxed mood. That is exactly when a person's guard drops, so it is the 'wound', the weak spot, of the year.

phrases.english: Avin said:
The wound of the year is the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אָבִין: סְקָבָא דְשַׁתָּא רִיגְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the setting where the barriers of אביי and רבא were most needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The festival is the most dangerous time for sin between men and women, so extra care is needed.

steps.title: Captive women stay in רב עמרם's house
steps.stepSummary: Redeemed captive women were housed upstairs at רב עמרם חסידא's house, and the ladder was taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some captive women who came to נהרדעא were brought up to the house of רב עמרם חסידא, and the ladder was removed from in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It sets the scene: women are sleeping upstairs, and the ladder is removed so no man can climb up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same safeguard רב ביבי asked for in step 19: take away the ladder. The story will show that even this safeguard can be tested by a strong desire.

phrases.english: Those captive women who came to Neharde'a.
They brought them up to the house of Rav Amram the Pious,
they removed the ladder from before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ שְׁבוּיָיתָא דַּאֲתַאי לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that illustrates how strong the danger is, connecting to the ladder in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: the women were upstairs with the ladder removed as a safeguard.

steps.title: רב עמרם is tempted and starts climbing
steps.stepSummary: Seeing one woman's beauty, רב עמרם lifts a huge ladder alone and starts to climb.
steps.simpleTranslation: When one of them passed by, a light shone in the opening. רב עמרם took a ladder that ten people could not lift, lifted it by himself, and started climbing.
steps.whatsHappening: The story's turning point: רב עמרם is overcome with desire and starts going up to the women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her beauty is described as light shining through the opening. His desire gives him impossible strength, lifting what ten men could not. This shows how powerful the יצר הרע can be, even for a חסיד.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening, a window or hatch

phrases.english: While one of them was passing by
a light fell in the opening.
phrases.notes: Her beauty was so great it looked like light shining through the opening.

phrases.english: Rav Amram took the ladder

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא הֲווֹ יָכְלִין בֵּי עַשְׂרָה לְמִדְלְיֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that ten people together could not lift,
he lifted it by himself,
and went climbing up.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָא חָלְפָה חֲדָא מִנַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the safeguard is about to fail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a great חסיד can be overpowered by desire, so safeguards matter.

steps.title: Halfway up, רב עמרם stops himself and cries fire
steps.stepSummary: Halfway up, רב עמרם braced himself and shouted 'Fire in עמרם's house!' to bring people.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the middle of the ladder, he braced himself and raised his voice: Fire in the house of עמרם!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם fights back against his desire by stopping and calling people over, knowing they would see him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He could not trust himself to stop alone, so he made sure he would be caught. Calling 'fire' brought people running, which made continuing impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: He braced himself, spread his legs to stop

phrases.english: When he reached the middle of the ladder
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the letter in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: he braced himself, raised his voice:
Fire in the house of Amram!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְפַלְגָא דְּדַרְגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The climax: רב עמרם turns back from sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When you can't stop yourself alone, bring in others to stop you, even at the cost of shame.

steps.title: The רבנן feel shamed, and רב עמרם answers
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן complained he embarrassed them, and רב עמרם answered that shame now is better than shame in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן came and said to him: You have embarrassed us. He said to them: Better that you be embarrassed by עמרם's house in this world and not be embarrassed by him in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן arrive, see what happened, and say he shamed them. רב עמרם explains why the shame was worth it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן felt that a great scholar being seen like this embarrassed them all. רב עמרם says a little shame in this world is far better than the lasting shame of sin in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: The Rabbis came, they said to him:
You have embarrassed us.
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: מוּטָב תִּיכַּסְפוּ בֵּי עַמְרָם בְּעָלְמָא הָדֵין
phrases.english: It is better that you be embarrassed by Amram's house in this world
and not be embarrassed by him in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ רַבָּנַן, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: כַּסֵּיפְתִּינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reaction to his shout and his reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shame in this world is worth accepting to avoid the shame of sin in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רב עמרם forces out his יצר הרע and declares victory
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם made his יצר הרע leave him; it came out like a pillar of fire, and he said he was stronger than it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made it swear to leave him, and it came out of him like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, and yet I am stronger than you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב עמרם driving out his יצר הרע and telling it that he beat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יצר הרע appears as a pillar of fire, showing how fierce it is. Yet רב עמרם, only flesh and blood, overcame it. The lesson is that a person can defeat even a very powerful desire.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it take an oath, he adjured it

steps.whatToRemember: The safeguards against יחוד are needed because desire is extremely strong, as רב עמרם's story shows. But a person who fights back can still win.

phrases.english: He adjured it that it should leave him,
phrases.notes: 'It' is his יצר הרע; the גמרא doesn't say the word but assumes it.

phrases.english: it came out of him like a pillar of fire.
He said to it: See,
that you are fire and I am flesh,
and I am stronger than you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁבְּעֵיהּ דְּיִנְפַּק מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with רב עמרם's victory.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The יצר הרע is fierce like fire, yet a person of flesh can overcome it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר is tested by a woman across the river
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר used to mock sinners. The שטן appeared to him as a woman across a river, and he grabbed a rope bridge and began crossing toward her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to make fun of people who sinned. One day the שטן appeared to him as a woman on the other side of the river. There was no ferry, so he grabbed hold of a rope bridge and started crossing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. רבי מאיר, who thought sinners were weak, is now being tempted himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבי מאיר looked down on sinners, as if fighting temptation were easy. The שטן shows him how strong the pull really is: even a great צדיק crosses a dangerous rope bridge to reach the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Appeared to him as, disguised himself as
The Satan, here meaning the יצר הרע
A rope stretched across the river

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הֲוָה מִתְלוֹצֵץ בְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir would mock those who commit sins.
One day, the Satan appeared to him
as a woman on the other side of the river.
There was no ferry,
so he took hold of a rope bridge and was crossing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הֲוָה מִתְלוֹצֵץ בְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב עמרם's victory over his יצר הרע, the גמרא brings another story about the strength of the יצר הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי מאיר, who mocked sinners, was drawn after temptation when the שטן tested him.

steps.title: Heaven's protection saves רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Halfway across, the שטן let go of רבי מאיר and said that only heaven's announcement to protect him and his Torah saved him from falling completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the middle of the rope bridge, the שטן let him go and said: If they weren't announcing in heaven, 'Be careful with רבי מאיר and his Torah,' I would have made your life worth two small coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The שטן stops the test and tells רבי מאיר that he was saved only because heaven protected him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר did not win by his own strength. He was saved from heaven because of his Torah. This answers his mocking of sinners: without heaven's help, he too would have sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: He let him go, left him
Two מעה, two small coins: worth almost nothing

steps.whatToRemember: Even a great צדיק cannot look down on sinners. רבי מאיר was saved from sin only because heaven protected him for the sake of his Torah.

phrases.english: When he reached halfway across the rope bridge,
he let him go and said:
phrases.notes: It's the שטן who lets go of רבי מאיר and speaks to him.

phrases.english: If not that they are announcing in heaven:
"Be careful with Rabbi Meir and his Torah,"
I would have made your blood worth two ma'ah.
phrases.notes: A מעה is a tiny coin. He means: I would have made your life worth almost nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא פַּלְגָא מִצְרָא שַׁבְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר was saved only by heavenly protection earned through his Torah, not by his own strength.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is tested by a woman atop a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא also mocked sinners. The שטן appeared to him as a woman at the top of a palm tree, and he started climbing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא used to make fun of people who sinned. One day the שטן appeared to him as a woman at the top of a palm tree. He grabbed the palm tree and started climbing up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that closely matches the first, now about רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats on purpose. Now there are two of the greatest תנאים, and both are shown to be vulnerable when tested. Climbing a tall palm tree, like crossing a rope bridge, shows how far the יצר הרע can pull a person.

keyTerms.meaning: The top of a palm tree

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֲוָה מִתְלוֹצֵץ בְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva would mock those who commit sins.
One day, the Satan appeared to him
as a woman at the top of a palm tree.
He grabbed the palm tree and began climbing up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֲוָה מִתְלוֹצֵץ בְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רבי מאיר's, with the same structure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא, who also mocked sinners, was drawn after temptation when tested.

steps.title: Heaven's protection saves רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Halfway up the tree, the שטן let go of רבי עקיבא and said that only heaven's announcement about him and his Torah saved him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the middle of the palm tree, the שטן let him go and said: If they weren't announcing in heaven, 'Be careful with רבי עקיבא and his Torah,' I would have made your life worth two small coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The second story ends exactly like the first. The שטן lets go and explains that heaven protected רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same lesson is repeated: Torah brings heavenly protection, but no person should think he is above temptation. Telling it twice makes the message stronger.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי מאיר and רבי עקיבא learned that resisting the יצר הרע is not easy. Their protection came from heaven because of their Torah.

phrases.english: When he reached halfway up the palm tree,
he let him go and said:
If not that they announce in heaven:
"Be careful with Rabbi Akiva and his Torah,"
I would have made your blood worth two ma'ah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְפַלְגֵיהּ דְּדִיקְלָא שַׁבְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the רבי עקיבא story with the same words as the end of the רבי מאיר story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא too was saved only by heavenly protection for his Torah.

steps.title: פלימו mocks the שטן, who comes as a poor man
steps.stepSummary: פלימו used to say every day, 'An arrow in the שטן's eye.' On ערב יום כיפור the שטן came to his door as a poor man, and they brought bread out to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: פלימו was used to saying every day: 'An arrow in the eye of the שטן!' One day, on ערב יום כיפור, the שטן appeared to him as a poor man. He came and called at the door, and they brought bread out to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third story, about פלימו. This time the test is not desire for a woman. The שטן comes as a poor man asking for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier figures, פלימו spoke as if the שטן were weak. Now the שטן comes to test him, disguised as a poor man asking for help on ערב יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום כיפור, the day before יום כיפור

phrases.aramaic: פְּלֵימוֹ הֲוָה רְגִיל לְמֵימַר כׇּל יוֹמָא
phrases.english: Peleimo was used to saying every day:
"An arrow in the eye of the Satan!"

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְכִיפּוּרֵי הֲוָה.
phrases.english: One day, it was the eve of Yom Kippur.
He appeared to him as a poor man.
He came and called at the door,
and they brought bread out to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלֵימוֹ הֲוָה רְגִיל לְמֵימַר כׇּל יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story about someone who made light of the שטן, now with a different kind of test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פלימו, who mocked the שטן daily, is visited by the שטן disguised as a poor man on ערב יום כיפור.

steps.title: The poor man asks to come inside
steps.stepSummary: The poor man complained about being left outside on such a day, so they brought him in and served him bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On a day like today, everyone is inside and I am outside? So he brought him in and they served him bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The poor man pushes for more. He is not happy eating at the door and gets himself invited into the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן moves step by step. Each request sounds fair on ערב יום כיפור, so פלימו keeps giving in. This slow pressure is the method of the test.

phrases.english: He said to him: On a day like today,
everyone is inside, and I am outside?
He brought him in, and they served him bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יוֹמָא כִּי הָאִידָּנָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא גַּוַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The poor man asks for more after receiving bread at the door.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor man is brought inside the house.

steps.title: The poor man asks to sit at the table
steps.stepSummary: The poor man complained about eating alone, so they sat him at the family table.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On a day like today, everyone is at the table and I am by myself? So they brought him and sat him at the table.
steps.whatsHappening: The poor man pushes one more step. Now he gets a seat at the family table itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same complaint, 'On a day like today,' repeats with a bigger request each time: from the door, to inside, to the table. The שטן has now come as close as possible to פלימו.

phrases.english: He said to him: On a day like today,
everyone is at the table, and I am by myself?
They brought him and sat him at the table.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יוֹמָא כִּי הָאִידָּנָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַתַּכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The poor man's third request, building on the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor man is seated at the family table.

steps.title: The poor man acts disgustingly at the table
steps.stepSummary: Sitting at the table, the poor man was covered in boils and sores and did disgusting things. פלימו begins to speak to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat there, his whole body full of boils and sores, and he was doing disgusting things with them. פלימו said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The poor man now sits at the table and behaves in a revolting way. The step ends with 'he said to him,' which sets up פלימו's words in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the real test shows. פלימו has to stay patient with a guest who is gross and embarrassing, at the table, on ערב יום כיפור. The גמרא stops right before telling us how פלימו reacts.

phrases.english: He was sitting, his whole body full of
boils and sores (on him),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and he was doing disgusting things with it.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is פלימו starting to speak. His words come next.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה יָתֵיב מְלָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ שִׁיחְנָא וְכִיבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once seated at the table, the poor man starts behaving in a revolting way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disguised שטן sits at פלימו's table covered in sores, acting disgustingly, setting up פלימו's response.
